lines: In this episode, we learn to read a cartridge, and to identify its calibre.
The aim is for you to be able to identify the correct ammunition for your firearm.

scenes.definition: The writing on the bottom of a cartridge, at the opposite end of the bullet. It shows the calibre of that cartridge.
lines: When you look at the bottom of a cartridge, the opposite end of the bullet, you will notice writing.
This is known as a headstamp.
On the headstamp, you will see the calibre printed for that particular cartridge.

scenes.caption: Cartridge identification: two headstamps
lines: Here are the two headstamps from the book.

lines.text: The top one shows the calibre, 38 SPL, and that it was manufactured by Federal.
lines.say: The top one shows the calibre, thirty-eight S P L, and that it was manufactured by Federal.

lines: Its plus P marking indicates more than normal pressure.

lines.text: The bottom one shows the manufacturer's name, WIN, and the calibre, 9 millimetre Luger.
lines.say: The bottom one shows the manufacturer's name, win, and the calibre, nine millimetre Luger.

scenes.definition: The diameter of the bullet, or the inside diameter of the barrel in which the bullet must travel.
lines: The term calibre means the diameter of the bullet.
Or the inside diameter of the barrel in which the bullet must travel.

scenes.heading: Matching ammunition to your firearm
bullets: Read the calibre on the headstamp
Check the calibre on your firearm license
Check the calibre on the slide or barrel
lines: First, determine the calibre of the ammunition from its headstamp.
Then look on your firearm license, which will also list the calibre for which you are licensed to carry.
Then look on the slide or barrel of the firearm, which will also show the calibre.

scenes.caption: Common handgun calibres
lines: The book shows thirteen common handgun calibres.

lines.text: From the left: 22 Short, 22 Long, 22 Magnum, 6.35 millimetre and 7.65 millimetre.
lines.say: From the left: twenty-two Short, twenty-two Long, twenty-two Magnum, six point three five millimetre, and seven point six five millimetre.

lines.text: Then 9 millimetre Short, 9 millimetre Parabellum, 38 Special and 357 Magnum.
lines.say: Then nine millimetre Short, nine millimetre Parabellum, thirty-eight Special, and three fifty-seven Magnum.

lines.text: And 40 S and W, 10 millimetre Auto, 44 Magnum and 45 ACP.
lines.say: And forty S and W, ten millimetre Auto, forty-four Magnum, and forty-five A C P.

lines: In your practical assessment, you will be required to identify the calibre of two different cartridges.
And to identify the correct ammunition for your own firearm.

scenes.caption: Hollow point bullets, and bullets before and after impact
lines: Here we see different types of hollow point bullets.
Hollow point bullets are also known as dum-dums.
Along the bottom are hollow point bullets before and after impact.

scenes.definition: Expand on impact. They cause a larger wound, but most importantly they are less likely to over-penetrate.
lines: Hollow point bullets expand on impact.
This will cause a larger wound.
But most importantly, they are less likely to over-penetrate.
The book says hollow point bullets are highly recommended for self defence.
